chunks: Yet they ascribe to jinns a partnership with God, although He created them; and they ascribe to Him sons and daughters, without possessing any knowledge. All praise be to Him. He is much too exalted for things they associate (with Him).
ai.seo_question: How do polytheists attribute partners to God according to Surah Al-An'am?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse critiques the pre-Islamic Arabs' anthropomorphic projection of their own lineage onto the Divine, specifically attributing the jinn as divine partners and claiming God begot sons and daughters. This 'without knowledge' (bi-ghayri 'ilm) highlights the irrationality of their idolatry, contrasting human limitation with God's absolute transcendence (Tanzih) from physical generation or companionship.
